criteria.label: Open source and licence
criteria.ours: Public application source under MIT. Inspect, modify and redistribute it subject to the licence and third-party notices. Open source does not mean every connected AI service is open source.

criteria.label: Bot or device capture
criteria.ours: Captures microphone and system audio on the computer. No meeting bot needs to join the call.

criteria.label: Platforms and installation
criteria.ours: Separate Mac and Windows technical betas. Mac: Apple Silicon, macOS 15+. Windows: x64, Windows 11 24H2+. Requirements and package features differ.

criteria.label: Local processing and offline use
criteria.ours: Audio capture and speech recognition run locally. Codex analysis can send selected conversation and repository excerpts to its AI service. The published beta is not an end-to-end offline AI product.

criteria.label: Can you keep the audio?
criteria.ours: Meeting recordings and transcript files are saved in the user directory. Local disk space and your backup policy determine retention.

criteria.label: Context beyond the transcript
criteria.ours: Read-only Codex search over selected local Git checkouts, documents, source and history. A repository connection is not a licence to upload everything.

criteria.label: Help during the call
criteria.ours: Near-live transcript and questions, risks and decisions. Ask Codex to check a statement against the selected working context.

criteria.label: Languages and switching mid-call
criteria.ours: Local ASR capabilities depend on the engine and build. Validate your language mix, accents and mid-call switches. New multilingual fixes in source are not automatically included in the pinned beta.

criteria.label: Who said what
criteria.ours: Speaker separation where available, with attribution that needs review. No independently verified speaker-accuracy score is claimed here.

criteria.label: Exports and connections
criteria.ours: Local HTML/PDF reports. Optional delivery to Drive, email and Telegram requires configuration. Newer source features must be checked against the installed release.

criteria.label: Cost and dependencies
criteria.ours: MIT application source. Budget separately for Codex access and any paid services you choose. This is not a promise that future hosted offerings will be free.

criteria.label: Setup and rollout trade-off
criteria.ours: Technical beta with prerequisites and OS permissions. The Mac package is not notarized, the Windows beta is unsigned, and automatic updates are not enabled in these pinned packages.

competitors.name: MeetScribe
competitors.title: MeetOnTrack vs MeetScribe: Meetily Roots & Open Source
competitors.description: Compare MeetOnTrack with MeetScribe: Meetily origins, open-source rights, local processing, live help, pricing and public beta limits. Official sources included.
competitors.summary: Both advertise bot-free meeting capture. The important questions are which product you are installing, what source rights it provides, and where processing happens. MeetScribe, Meetily Community and Meetily PRO are not interchangeable products.
competitors.short: A Meetily-derived service: separate upstream source rights from the product you install.
competitors.chooseOurs: You want inspectable application source, retained local audio and live checks against selected working repositories. You accept a technical beta and its documented installation limits rather than assuming every source-tree feature has shipped.
competitors.chooseTheirs: You want the team summaries and follow-up integrations MeetScribe advertises. Trial the actual workflow before relying on the feature list.
competitors.tradeoffTitle: MeetScribe is based on Meetily, but it is not Meetily
competitors.tradeoff: MeetScribe credits Zackriya Solutions' Meeting Minutes as its foundation; that repository now redirects to Meetily. The upstream repository has an MIT licence and documents local Whisper/Parakeet transcription, Ollama summaries and optional external AI providers. It describes PRO as a separate codebase. Those upstream capabilities and source rights do not establish the capabilities or licence of the complete MeetScribe distribution. MeetScribe's third-party notices are attribution, not a published full-product source grant.
competitors.test: Install the exact candidate on your own OS. Test a short multilingual call, replay and export, then inspect processing destinations with external AI disabled. Ask the vendor to resolve its processing and plan descriptions before using sensitive recordings. Do not infer offline behavior from an upstream project or a marketing illustration.

open-source.text: MeetScribe acknowledges its open-source foundation. Its service terms restrict reverse engineering; a source repository and licence for the complete MeetScribe product were not verified. Meetily's MIT licence is a separate upstream fact.

capture.text: The FAQ describes device-audio capture without a meeting bot, despite auto-join wording elsewhere on the homepage.

platforms.text: Mac and Windows download links are offered. We have not installed or tested these packages.

processing.text: The homepage says audio processing is local. The privacy policy describes audio streams processed and discarded, not permanently stored on servers. That wording leaves processing location unclear; fully offline operation is not established.

recordings.text: The privacy policy describes retained transcripts and summaries and non-permanent server audio. A replayable local audio archive is not established by that policy.

context.text: Calendar and productivity integrations are advertised. Search across local folders or Git history was not verified.

live.text: Advertises live transcription and action extraction. Repository-grounded statement checking was not verified.

languages.text: A supported-language matrix and mid-call language-switching behavior were not verified in the reviewed pages. Test your language mix.

speakers.text: Advertises speaker detection; we have not benchmarked its attribution accuracy.

export.text: Terms allow data export before termination but do not enumerate formats. Verify the actual files and workflow you need.

cost.text: Pricing describes one Pro plan; the FAQ also describes a free plan. Confirm current allowances at signup.

readiness.text: Certain features require an account and subscription. The terms disclaim guaranteed AI accuracy. No comparative installation, performance or compliance audit was performed for this article.

competitors.name: Granola
competitors.title: MeetOnTrack vs Granola: Open Source & Local Control
competitors.description: Compare MeetOnTrack and Granola on open source, audio retention, cloud processing, local Git context, languages and setup. Sources and beta limits included.
competitors.summary: Choose between an open-source, locally stored recording workflow and Granola's managed AI notepad. Both offer bot-free capture. Keeping the original audio and inspecting the application source are the more useful dividing lines.
competitors.short: Bot-free notes and meeting memory vs retained local recordings and inspectable source.
competitors.chooseOurs: You want to retain the meeting audio, inspect or adapt the application, and check what is said against documents and Git history already on your computer. You are comfortable with a technical beta and managing the AI connection yourself.
competitors.chooseTheirs: You want a managed notepad that improves your notes, searches meeting history and supports sharing across devices. You prefer the vendor to operate the service and do not need a retained audio recording in Granola.
competitors.tradeoffTitle: A notepad is not an audio archive
competitors.tradeoff: Granola's no-stored-audio approach can be useful when your policy favors retaining text rather than recordings. MeetOnTrack makes a different choice: it keeps local media so you can return to the original. Neither choice is universally more private. Decide what must be retained, where it may be processed and who may receive it.
competitors.test: If audio replay is essential, verify that you can keep and reopen the original recording. If it is prohibited, verify your retention policy before enabling local recording. Then test note quality on your own terminology rather than relying on a generic accuracy claim.

open-source.text: A full-product open-source licence was not verified in the reviewed sources. API or MCP access alone does not grant rights to modify and redistribute the application.

capture.text: Bot-free device-audio capture. Its security guide describes manually starting transcription rather than an auto-joining bot.

platforms.text: Vendor lists macOS, Windows, iOS and Android. A managed desktop/mobile notepad workflow.

processing.text: Uses external transcription and AI providers. Notes are stored in its AWS cloud infrastructure. Device capture does not mean offline processing.

recordings.text: Does not retain a replayable meeting-audio archive. Desktop transcribes live; mobile temporarily caches audio for transcription. Transcripts and notes are retained.

context.text: Meeting memory, calendar preparation, integrations, API and MCP. Read-only search of local Git checkout history is not established by these sources.

live.text: AI notes and chat around meeting context. It is not just a static transcript viewer.

languages.text: Multi-language support is listed in the plans. Confirm your specific language pair and switching behavior in a real trial.

speakers.text: Speaker tagging is included in its feature matrix. Tagging is not an independent guarantee of correct attribution.

export.text: Shared folders and integrations. Advanced integrations and administrative controls depend on plan.

cost.text: Free Basic and paid per-user plans. History, AI features and integration allowances vary. Use current pricing rather than assuming a free plan includes everything.

readiness.text: Managed product with desktop/mobile apps and business/enterprise controls listed by plan. Evaluate your own permissions and security requirements.

competitors.name: Fireflies.ai
competitors.title: MeetOnTrack vs Fireflies.ai: Capture, Context & Source
competitors.description: MeetOnTrack vs Fireflies.ai: open source, bot and bot-free capture, retained audio, live assistance, languages, integrations and beta trade-offs.
competitors.summary: Fireflies.ai offers both a meeting bot and system-audio capture, including live assistance. The decision is not simply bot versus no bot: compare the capture mode, retained media, working context and control over the software.
competitors.short: A managed meeting workspace with several capture modes vs a local, open-source workflow.
competitors.chooseOurs: You want application source you can inspect, locally retained recordings and answers grounded in selected local repositories. You can accept the setup and operational responsibility of a technical beta.
competitors.chooseTheirs: You want a managed meeting workspace, meeting-bot options, team integrations and a live assistant in the vendor's workflow. You prefer plan-based controls and vendor-operated infrastructure to maintaining your own stack.
competitors.tradeoffTitle: Compare the capture mode, not just the brand
competitors.tradeoff: Fireflies' desktop guide separates bot capture from no-bot system-audio capture. It lists retained audio/video and named speaker attribution for the bot, while no-bot capture uses generic numbered speakers without saved audio/video. Live Assist is available in both. Test the exact capture mode if replay or attribution matters.
competitors.test: Run the same short call once with the bot and once with system audio. Check which files are retained, how names are attached to utterances and whether the live answer cites the right source. Do not treat the feature list for one mode as evidence for the other.

open-source.text: Commercial software and service licence. The reviewed terms are not a full-product open-source licence. API availability does not change that distinction.

capture.text: Both a visible meeting bot and no-bot system-audio capture are documented. Bot-free capture is not unique to MeetOnTrack.

platforms.text: Desktop, mobile, browser and meeting integrations are listed. Select the supported capture method for your device and meeting app.

processing.text: Vendor-managed cloud service. Dedicated/private storage options are not the same as local speech recognition or a fully offline application.

recordings.text: The desktop guide lists saved audio/video with bot capture, but no saved audio/video for no-bot system-audio capture. Confirm the current mode before relying on replay.

context.text: Meeting search, AskFred, integrations and broader assistant features. Local Git checkout/history inspection is not established by the reviewed pages.

live.text: Live Assist, transcripts, AI notes and AskFred are documented for both bot and system-audio capture.

languages.text: Automatic detection and a multi-language mode are listed. Verify the applicable plan, capture path and your language combination.

speakers.text: The desktop guide distinguishes bot speaker labels from no-bot numbered speakers. Do not assume named attribution in every capture mode.

export.text: Transcript/recording downloads, team collaboration, integrations and API are listed. Allowances depend on plan and capture mode.

cost.text: Free and paid per-seat tiers, with separate feature, storage and AI allowances. Check live pricing and any add-ons.

readiness.text: Managed workspace with team and enterprise options. Broader integrations may fit teams that do not want to maintain a local beta.

competitors.name: Bluedot
competitors.title: MeetOnTrack vs Bluedot: Open Source & Meeting Data
competitors.description: Compare MeetOnTrack and Bluedot on open source, bot-free recording, local versus cloud data, languages, work context, exports and pricing structure.
competitors.summary: Both tools offer bot-free capture. Bluedot focuses on a managed, shared meeting library and post-meeting workflows. MeetOnTrack emphasizes inspectable source, local recordings and checking the conversation against your local working context.
competitors.short: Bot-free capture and a shared cloud library vs local files and read-only repository context.
competitors.chooseOurs: You want locally retained meeting files and a workflow you can modify under MIT. Your live questions depend on documents, code or Git history in repositories already on your machine.
competitors.chooseTheirs: You want bot-free recording connected to a shared meeting library and downstream CRM or collaboration workflows. You prefer a vendor-managed service with workspace governance rather than running the technical beta yourself.
competitors.tradeoff: Bluedot captures through the browser or desktop without joining as a bot, while its security documentation describes AWS data storage. That is a cloud workflow with device capture. MeetOnTrack retains files locally, but configured Codex analysis can still send excerpts to an AI provider. Decide separately where capture, transcription, storage and analysis are allowed to happen.
competitors.test: Use a call that includes your real conferencing app and language mix. Check the retained recording, the transcript after a language switch and the destination of a shared report. For long calls, check the recording-duration limit of the exact Bluedot plan you are considering.

open-source.text: Commercial service terms, not a full-product open-source licence. An available API or MCP integration does not provide the application's source licence.

capture.text: Bot-free browser and desktop capture. No extra participant is required for its documented capture workflow.

platforms.text: Chrome, Mac and Windows desktop, plus mobile options are listed by the vendor.

processing.text: Vendor-managed processing and AWS storage. Its no-training commitments are distinct from a promise of offline processing.

recordings.text: Recordings live in the managed library. Audio/video options, recording duration and retention controls vary by plan.

context.text: Searchable shared meeting history and CRM/collaboration connections. Read-only local Git history search is not established by these sources.

live.text: The reviewed product pages emphasize capture, summaries and post-meeting automation. A repository-grounded live assistant is not verified here.

languages.text: Automatic language selection and many transcription languages are documented. Its help guide describes limits when changing transcript languages, so test your mixed-language workflow.

speakers.text: Speaker attribution quality for your exact device/capture path is not established by the sources used here. Verify it in a trial rather than reading this as a missing feature.

export.text: Share links, clips and downstream integrations. API/MCP and CRM features have plan-dependent availability.

cost.text: The Free plan lists five lifetime meetings. Paid per-user plans expand recording and workflow allowances. Check the billing period and duration limits.

readiness.text: Managed apps and workspace controls, including enterprise governance options on eligible plans.

competitors.name: tl;dv
competitors.title: MeetOnTrack vs tl;dv: Open Source, Recording & Context
competitors.description: MeetOnTrack vs tl;dv: compare open source, bot-free capture, recording storage, multilingual calls, local Git context and team workflows with sources.
competitors.summary: tl;dv combines recording, a shared meeting library and team workflows, and now offers bot-free desktop capture too. MeetOnTrack is a different fit when local media, open-source control and inspecting local working documents matter more than a managed collaboration suite.
competitors.short: Shared meeting evidence and team workflows vs open-source control and local work context.
competitors.chooseOurs: You want to inspect or adapt the application and retain the meeting files under your own local storage policy. Your assistant needs to check specific repository documents or code history while you talk.
competitors.chooseTheirs: You want a vendor-managed meeting library, cross-meeting questions and sales or team workflows. You prefer shared cloud access and integrations to operating a local technical beta.
competitors.tradeoffTitle: A free recording plan is not unlimited everything
competitors.tradeoff: tl;dv offers a free entry point, but its own materials describe plan-dependent AI features, exports and retention, plus fair-use limits. Compare the exact plan and capture mode. Bot recordings and audio-only desktop capture do not necessarily provide the same media or speaker names.
competitors.test: Try a conversation that switches languages and confirm that the chosen plan supports that workflow. Inspect the export formats and video-retention period before adopting it as a long-term archive. Compare named attribution in bot and audio-only recordings.

open-source.text: Commercial service terms, not a full-product open-source licence. Integration/API access should not be confused with rights to modify and redistribute the product.

capture.text: Bot recording and a bot-free desktop path are available. Older comparisons that describe tl;dv as bot-only are incomplete.

platforms.text: Desktop downloads for Mac and Windows and a Chrome extension. Native-mobile-app availability is not established here; vendor pages differ on mobile options.

processing.text: Managed cloud processing and storage. Its security page describes European hosting, not an on-device-only transcription product.

recordings.text: A managed recording library. Retained media and speaker names differ between bot and audio-only capture. Retention and export permissions depend on plan.

context.text: Meeting-library search, cross-meeting AI and connected team tools. Local Git checkout/history search is not established by these sources.

live.text: Meeting capture and timestamped notes are documented. Repository-grounded live statement checking is not verified by these sources.

languages.text: Multilingual transcription and automatic mid-call switching are described. The vendor places multi-language meetings and premium transcription on Business in its current guide.

speakers.text: Bot capture provides speaker-labelled transcripts. Audio-only recordings can show numbered speakers unless linked to calendar context. Verify the selected mode.

export.text: Sharing, clips, collaboration and workflow integrations. Its guide notes transcript export-format limitations, so verify the format you actually need.

cost.text: Free entry plan and paid tiers. AI, exports, retention and fair-use allowances need checking alongside the advertised recording allowance.

readiness.text: Managed collaboration and sales workflows. A better fit when the shared workspace matters more than maintaining local application source.
